function: CSI feedback: an autoencoder compresses the CSI into a latent vector that shape-gain vector quantization (VQ-VAE) turns into a finite-bit feedback for the base station (p. 3).
system: FDD massive MIMO: BS with 32-antenna ULA, single-antenna UE, OFDM with 1024 subcarriers; no RIS; 5.3 GHz indoor and 300 MHz outdoor (p. 3, 8).
method: VQ-VAE autoencoder with shape-gain quantization (clipped mu-law gain, trainable Grassmannian shape codebook) and nested multi-rate codebook; trained offline end to end on reconstruction loss (p. 4-8).
data_channel: COST2100 channel model, indoor picocellular 5.3 GHz and outdoor rural 300 MHz, default settings of [15]; 100000 training, 30000 validation, 20000 test samples (p. 8-9).
test_conditions: Results reported per scenario (indoor, outdoor) on a held-out test set at several feedback overheads; no cross-scenario, band or antenna-count test (p. 9-10).
baselines: Learned only: original VQ-VAE [11], DL methods of [3] and [16] (indoor), [3] and [17] (outdoor); single-rate variant of the proposal. No non-learned baseline compared (p. 9-10).
metrics: NMSE in dB versus feedback overhead in bits; quantization complexity as number of multiplications versus NMSE (p. 9-10).
complexity: Quantization complexity order O(2^max{Bmag,Bdir}) versus O(2^B) for VQ-VAE (p. 5); number of multiplications plotted against NMSE, Fig. 3 (p. 10).
